**JYP Entertainment Corporation** ([Korean](/wiki/Korean_language "Korean language"): JYP 엔터테인먼트) is a South Korean [multinational](/wiki/Multinational_corporation "Multinational corporation") [entertainment](/wiki/Entertainment "Entertainment") and [record label](/wiki/Record_label "Record label") [conglomerate](/wiki/Conglomerate_(company) "Conglomerate (company)") founded in 1997 by [J.Y. Park](/wiki/J.Y._Park "J.Y. Park"). Operating as a record label, talent agency, music production company, event management company, concert production company and music publishing house, it is one of the largest entertainment companies in South Korea. The company also operates subsidiary ventures and divisions internationally.

## History

### 1997–99: Formation and first generation K-pop artists

JYP Entertainment was founded in 1997 by South Korean singer-songwriter [Park Jin-young](/wiki/J.Y._Park "J.Y. Park") as Tae-Hong Planning Corporation. In 2001, the company was retitled as JYP Entertainment, named after his stage name, J. Y. Park.[[7]](#cite_note-7) In 1997, the company signed its first artist – [Pearl](/wiki/Pearl_(singer) "Pearl (singer)").

In 1999, entertainment company [SidusHQ](/wiki/IHQ_(company) "IHQ (company)") introduced the future members of boy band [g.o.d](/wiki/G.o.d "G.o.d") to Park, as their producer and mentor. In cooperation with SidusHQ, JYP Entertainment oversaw the formation of g.o.d, which would make their debut appearance on January 13, 1999.[[8]](#cite_note-8) The group was managed by SidusHQ, with their first album, *[Chapter 1](/wiki/Chapter_1_(g.o.d_album) "Chapter 1 (g.o.d album)")*, being produced by Park.[[9]](#cite_note-9)

### 2000–09: Early success and second generation K-pop artists

In December 2000, JYP Entertainment signed [Rain](/wiki/Rain_(entertainer) "Rain (entertainer)") as a trainee, who made his debut two years later in May 2002.[[12]](#cite_note-12)[[13]](#cite_note-13) Rain would then rise to become a commercial success throughout and beyond Asia,[[14]](#cite_note-multiple-14) which was seen when his third studio album, *[It's Raining](/wiki/It%27s_Raining_(album) "It's Raining (album)")*, went on to record cumulative sales of over 1 million copies in seven Asian countries, including South Korea.[[15]](#cite_note-15)

On December 27, 2002, the company's first boy group was a four-member vocal oriented group, [Noel](/wiki/Noel_(band) "Noel (band)"), which failed to attract popularity. The company then turned its focus towards the duo brothers [One Two](/w/index.php?title=One_Two&action=edit&redlink=1 "One Two (page does not exist)") [[ko](https://ko.wikipedia.org/wiki/%EC%9B%90%ED%88%AC "ko:원투")] in 2003. In 2004, after the boy band [g.o.d](/wiki/G.o.d "G.o.d")'s group contract with SidusHQ ended, they signed a contract with JYP Entertainment.[[16]](#cite_note-16) Other artists that debuted under JYP Entertainment, from 2000 to 2005 were [Park Ji-yoon](/wiki/Park_Ji-yoon "Park Ji-yoon"), [Byul](/wiki/Byul "Byul"), [Lim Jeong-hee](/wiki/Lim_Jeong-hee "Lim Jeong-hee"), [Ryanga Rhanga](/w/index.php?title=Ryanga_Rhanga&action=edit&redlink=1 "Ryanga Rhanga (page does not exist)") [[ko](https://ko.wikipedia.org/wiki/%EB%9F%89%ED%98%84%EB%9F%89%ED%95%98 "ko:량현량하")], and [Ivy](/wiki/Ivy_(South_Korean_singer) "Ivy (South Korean singer)").

In May 2006, the company formed its first girl group, [Wonder Girls](/wiki/Wonder_Girls "Wonder Girls"),[[17]](#cite_note-17) who became a commercial success and was the first South Korean group to enter the [*Billboard* Hot 100](/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") in 2009, with their song "[Nobody](/wiki/Nobody_(Wonder_Girls_song) "Nobody (Wonder Girls song)")".[[18]](#cite_note-billboard-18) Their success lead to a management deal with the [Jonas Group](/wiki/Nine_West_Holdings "Nine West Holdings"), which led the group to open the [Jonas Brothers](/wiki/Jonas_Brothers "Jonas Brothers")' [world tour](/wiki/Jonas_Brothers_World_Tour_2009 "Jonas Brothers World Tour 2009") in select cities.[[19]](#cite_note-jobro-19)

In 2007, Rain left JYP Entertainment and established his own agency called [J. Tune Entertainment](/wiki/J._Tune_Entertainment "J. Tune Entertainment").[[20]](#cite_note-:2-20)

In 2008, the competitive reality series *Hot Blood Men* aired, pitting male trainees against each other for the chance to debut.[[23]](#cite_note-23) The winning group, [One Day](/wiki/One_Day_(South_Korean_band) "One Day (South Korean band)"), was later split into two boy bands, [2PM](/wiki/2PM "2PM") and [2AM](/wiki/2AM_(band) "2AM (band)"). Both debuted in the same year.[[24]](#cite_note-24) 2AM was jointly contracted with [Big Hit Entertainment](/wiki/Big_Hit_Music "Big Hit Music").[[25]](#cite_note-:0-25) Later in October, the JYP Beijing Center was opened, as the company's China branch. In that same year, the [Creative Artists Agency](/wiki/Creative_Artists_Agency "Creative Artists Agency") included JYP Entertainment in its roster of high-profile clientele.[[26]](#cite_note-26)[[27]](#cite_note-27)

Expanding its endeavors into the drama production industry following in the footsteps of SM Entertainment Group's [SM C&C](/wiki/SM_Culture_%26_Contents "SM Culture & Contents") and CJ E&M's [Studio Dragon](/wiki/Studio_Dragon "Studio Dragon") – JYP Entertainment jointly established the television drama production company Holym with Key East Entertainment in June 2009.[[28]](#cite_note-28) Holym later announced its first major television drama production, *[Dream High](/wiki/Dream_High "Dream High")*, in 2010, starring artists from JYP Entertainment.[[29]](#cite_note-29)[[30]](#cite_note-30)

### 2010–17: Joint ventures and third generation K-pop artists

In March 2010, JYP Entertainment made a joint venture with [SM Entertainment](/wiki/SM_Entertainment "SM Entertainment"), [YG Entertainment](/wiki/YG_Entertainment "YG Entertainment"), [Star Empire Entertainment](/wiki/Star_Empire_Entertainment "Star Empire Entertainment"), Media Line, CAN Entertainment and Music Factory Entertainment to establish KMP Holdings, the official distributor of releases from these companies.[[31]](#cite_note-31) On December 28, 2010, JYP Entertainment became the largest shareholder of [J. Tune Entertainment](/wiki/J._Tune_Entertainment "J. Tune Entertainment").[[20]](#cite_note-:2-20)[[32]](#cite_note-:3-32) The subsidiary AQ Entertainment was later formed and introduced the Chinese-Korean girl group [Miss A](/wiki/Miss_A "Miss A").

In November 2011, the American based subsidiary JYP Creative was established. Park invested approximately US$1.2 million in the branch. After a year of operation, the company saw a net loss of around US$1.5 million by the end of 2012, leading to the liquidation and closure of the branch, including the New York branch.[[34]](#cite_note-34) The same year, [Park Jimin](/wiki/Jamie_(singer) "Jamie (singer)"), winner of the competitive TV series *[K-pop Star](/wiki/K-pop_Star_season_1 "K-pop Star season 1")* and [Baek Yerin](/wiki/Baek_Yerin "Baek Yerin"), a female trainee and contestant on the show *[Star King](/wiki/Star_King_(TV_program) "Star King (TV program)")*, debuted as the duo [15&](/wiki/15%26 "15&").[[35]](#cite_note-35)[*[unreliable source?](/wiki/Wikipedia:Reliable_sources "Wikipedia:Reliable sources")*]

In 2012, JYP Pictures signed a contract with China Eastern Performing Arts Group to co-produce a movie *Hold Your Hand*, featuring actors who were signed to JYP Entertainment.[[36]](#cite_note-36)

On June 20, 2013, the merger plan for the [publicly listed](/wiki/Public_company "Public company") JYP Entertainment and the [non-listed](/wiki/Private_company "Private company") JYP was announced.[[37]](#cite_note-37)[[38]](#cite_note-38) The merger was approved on October 17.[[39]](#cite_note-39) Miss A and [Baek A-yeon](/wiki/Baek_A-yeon "Baek A-yeon"), also joined JYP Entertainment due to the merger.[[40]](#cite_note-AQEntertainment-40)[[41]](#cite_note-41) On August 25, 2013, JYP Entertainment and [KeyEast](/wiki/KeyEast "KeyEast") terminated their joint production enterprise, Holym.[[42]](#cite_note-42)[*[unreliable source?](/wiki/Wikipedia:Reliable_sources "Wikipedia:Reliable sources")*] On November 17, 2013, the company partnered with [Smilegate](/wiki/Smilegate "Smilegate") to promote the video game *[Crossfire](/wiki/Crossfire_(2007_video_game) "Crossfire (2007 video game)")* with [2PM](/wiki/2PM "2PM") and [Miss A](/wiki/Miss_A "Miss A").[[43]](#cite_note-43)

In January 2014, the seven talent agencies behind [KMP Holdings](/wiki/KMP_Holdings "KMP Holdings") formed a collective bond partnership and bought 13.48% of [KT Music](/wiki/KT_Music "KT Music")'s stocks, leaving [KT Corporation](/wiki/KT_Corporation "KT Corporation") with 49.99%.[[44]](#cite_note-gaonchart1-44) In the same month, [Got7](/wiki/Got7 "Got7"), made their debut.[[45]](#cite_note-kpopherald-45)[[46]](#cite_note-46) 2AM's joint contract of [Big Hit Entertainment](/wiki/Big_Hit_Entertainment "Big Hit Entertainment") with JYP Entertainment later in April ended, after three of the 2AM members returned to JYP Entertainment, and member [Lee Chang-min](/wiki/Lee_Chang-min_(singer) "Lee Chang-min (singer)") stayed with Big Hit Entertainment, to continue his career and as part of the duo [Homme](/wiki/Homme_(duo) "Homme (duo)").[[25]](#cite_note-:0-25) In August, JYP Pictures and Dongyang World Culture Communication produced the drama *Dream Knight*, starring Got7 members.[[47]](#cite_note-47) Season three *[K-pop Star](/wiki/K-pop_Star "K-pop Star")* winner [Bernard Park](/wiki/Bernard_Park "Bernard Park") signed a contract with JYP Entertainment to start his solo career, and making his debut on October 6.[[48]](#cite_note-48) On December 17, J.Y. Park sold the company's headquarters building in [Cheongdam-dong](/wiki/Cheongdam-dong "Cheongdam-dong"), Seoul to Choi Ki-won, for approximately $7 million, on the term that JYP Entertainment will still use the building for three years on rent.[[49]](#cite_note-49)[[50]](#cite_note-50)

The subsidiary [Studio J](/wiki/Studio_J "Studio J") was formed on January 9, 2015, in line with JYP Entertainment's goal to "promote free and deep artists that create authentic music rather than appealing to the mainstream demand." The first artist on Studio J's roster was [G.Soul](/wiki/G.Soul "G.Soul"), who debuted on the same day.[[53]](#cite_note-StudioJ-53)[[54]](#cite_note-StudioJ2-54) In March, 2AM members [Seulong](/wiki/Lim_Seul-ong "Lim Seul-ong") and [Jin-woon](/wiki/Jeong_Jin-woon "Jeong Jin-woon") departed from the company following their contracts' expiration, while [Jo Kwon](/wiki/Jo_Kwon "Jo Kwon") renewed his contract. The company stated 2AM remained intact and would be promoting as a group.[[55]](#cite_note-2AM-55) On April 15, the company signed a contract with Jax Coco, a Hong Kong-based coconut product company. Both companies planned to launch coconut oil, coconut flakes, and other related products at major department stores and supermarkets in South Korea.[[56]](#cite_note-56) In September, rock band [Day6](/wiki/Day6 "Day6") debuted.[[57]](#cite_note-57) In October, the girl group [Twice](/wiki/Twice "Twice") debuted. The members of the group were chosen from the competitive reality show *[Sixteen](/wiki/Sixteen_(TV_program) "Sixteen (TV program)")*.[[58]](#cite_note-58)

In February 2016, JYP Entertainment established a music distribution partnership with China Music Corporation.[[59]](#cite_note-59) It was followed by JYP Entertainment jointly establishing Beijing Xin Sheng Entertainment Co. Ltd. with [Tencent Music](/wiki/Tencent_Music "Tencent Music") in the same year,[[60]](#cite_note-qdaily.com-60) which oversaw the debut of the Chinese boy band [Boy Story](/wiki/Boy_Story "Boy Story").[[61]](#cite_note-61)

In July 2017, JYP Entertainment acquired a property worth 20.2 billion KRW in [Seongnae-dong](/wiki/Seongnae-dong "Seongnae-dong"), [Gangdong District](/wiki/Gangdong_District "Gangdong District"), Seoul to be used as its new office.[[62]](#cite_note-62) A partnership with [Dailymotion](/wiki/Dailymotion "Dailymotion"), Europe's largest video platform, was signed to open its artist channel on its platform to secure a more global fan base.[[63]](#cite_note-63)[[64]](#cite_note-64)

### 2018–present: Further success and fourth generation K-pop artists

On January 31, 2018, JYP Entertainment entered into a music business agreement with SM Entertainment, [Big Hit Entertainment](/wiki/Big_Hit_Entertainment "Big Hit Entertainment"), and [SK Telecom](/wiki/SK_Telecom "SK Telecom") to launch a new music platform Flo, which will utilize various new technologies such as artificial intelligence and 5G networking. SK Telecom affiliate [Iriver Inc](/wiki/Iriver_Inc "Iriver Inc") would be responsible for handling the music distribution.[[65]](#cite_note-65)[[66]](#cite_note-66)[[67]](#cite_note-67) In the first half of 2018, JYP Entertainment became the second largest entertainment company in South Korea, mainly due to the success of [Twice](/wiki/Twice "Twice") and [Got7](/wiki/Got7 "Got7").[[68]](#cite_note-68) On March 26, a new boy group [Stray Kids](/wiki/Stray_Kids "Stray Kids") debuted, named after the 2017 reality show of the same title.[[69]](#cite_note-69) In May, the company became the sole South Korean entertainment company to rank in [Financial Times](/wiki/Financial_Times "Financial Times") magazine's "FT 1000: High-Growth Companies Asia-Pacific" list.[[70]](#cite_note-70) On August 30, the company's shares closed at 31,300 KRW, pushing the company's market capitalization to 1.09 trillion KRW.[[52]](#cite_note-:1-52)

On January 21, 2019, JYP Entertainment announced its next girl group, [Itzy](/wiki/Itzy "Itzy"). The group released their debut single album, *It'z Different* in February, featuring the single "Dalla Dalla".[[71]](#cite_note-71) On January 24, the program *Super Intern* premiered on Mnet, which featured the internship process at JYP Entertainment, with the goal of turning the interns into permanent marketing management staff.[[72]](#cite_note-72) The show premiered on Mnet on January 24. On January 29, plans of creating a Japanese girl group, under their vision "JYP 2.0: Globalization By Localization" was announced.[[73]](#cite_note-73) On the season finale of *[Nizi Project](/wiki/Nizi_Project_season_1 "Nizi Project season 1")*, the line-up for the new girl group, [NiziU](/wiki/NiziU "NiziU"), was revealed. The group is a partnership with [Sony Music Entertainment Japan](/wiki/Sony_Music_Entertainment_Japan "Sony Music Entertainment Japan"), for its activities in Japan.[[74]](#cite_note-74)[[75]](#cite_note-75) The group made their debut on December 2, 2020.[[76]](#cite_note-76) On March 11, 2019, JYP Entertainment made a partnership with Sony Music Entertainment's [The Orchard](/wiki/The_Orchard_(company) "The Orchard (company)"). JYP Entertainment would distribute both digital and physical releases to key markets in the internationally through The Orchard in order to "expand the label's presence around the world."[[77]](#cite_note-77) On June 8, Fanling Culture Media trainee [Yao Chen](/wiki/R1SE "R1SE") placed 5th in the finale of *[Produce Camp 2019](/wiki/Produce_Camp_2019 "Produce Camp 2019")* has made the final lineup of project group [R1SE](/wiki/R1SE "R1SE"). The group made their debut on the same day.[[78]](#cite_note-78) On June 17, JYP and [Make-A-Wish Korea](/wiki/Make-A-Wish_Foundation "Make-A-Wish Foundation") signed a memorandum of understanding to help support children's wishes under JYP Entertainment's "Every Dream Matters!" campaign as part of their [corporate social responsibility](/wiki/Corporate_social_responsibility "Corporate social responsibility"). Under the agreement, the company would be carrying out various social responsibility activities with its artists, employees and fans in order to support campaigns and initiatives for children with incurable diseases.[[79]](#cite_note-79) On July 24, JYP Entertainment announced the closure of their acting division and would jointly manage its actors with the new start-up company, Npio Entertainment, created by JYP Entertainment Vice President Pyo Jong-rok. Actors [Jang Hee-ryung](/wiki/Jang_Hee-ryung "Jang Hee-ryung"), [Park Si-eun](/wiki/Park_Si-eun_(actress,_born_2001) "Park Si-eun (actress, born 2001)") and [Ryu Won](/wiki/Ryu_Won "Ryu Won") left the company. Actors [Yoon Park](/wiki/Yoon_Park "Yoon Park"), [Kang Hoon](/wiki/Kang_Hoon "Kang Hoon"), [Shin Ye-eun](/wiki/Shin_Ye-eun "Shin Ye-eun"), [Kim Dong-hee](/wiki/Kim_Dong-hee_(actor) "Kim Dong-hee (actor)") and Lee Chan-sun stayed in the company for the remainder of their contract periods.[[80]](#cite_note-Npio-80)[[81]](#cite_note-:4-81)

On January 6, 2020, [Shinhan Card](/wiki/Shinhan_Card "Shinhan Card") collaborated with JYP Entertainment to release four "JYP Fan's EDM Check Cards" – JYP, Got7, Day6 and Twice. Certain percentages of the amount used when making payments using the check cards were to be donated to Make-A-Wish Korea.[[82]](#cite_note-82) On February 24, Twice was signed under [Republic Records](/wiki/Republic_Records "Republic Records") for American promotions.[[83]](#cite_note-83) On August 4, a collaboration with SM Entertainment to establish Beyond Live Corporation, a joint company for virtual concerts was announced.[[84]](#cite_note-84)[[85]](#cite_note-85) On November 17, JYP Entertainment invested 5 billion KRW in [Naver Z](/wiki/Naver_Corporation "Naver Corporation"), the developer of the online avatar app Zepeto.[[86]](#cite_note-86)

On January 10, 2021, all members of Got7 left JYP Entertainment upon the completion of their 7-year contract.[[87]](#cite_note-87) On April 26, JYP Entertainment and [P Nation](/wiki/P_Nation "P Nation") announced to form their new boy group in *[Loud](/wiki/Loud_(TV_program) "Loud (TV program)")*. It premiered on June 5 on [SBS](/wiki/Seoul_Broadcasting_System "Seoul Broadcasting System").[[88]](#cite_note-88) On July 12, the second season of *[Nizi Project](/wiki/Nizi_Project "Nizi Project")* was announced as a Global Boys Audition.[[89]](#cite_note-oricon_2021-07-13-89) On November 1, JYP Entertainment announced its new rock band [Xdinary Heroes](/wiki/Xdinary_Heroes "Xdinary Heroes"). The band released their debut single "[Happy Death Day](/wiki/Happy_Death_Day_(song) "Happy Death Day (song)")" on December 6.[[90]](#cite_note-90)[[91]](#cite_note-91)

On January 26, 2022, a new girl group [Nmixx](/wiki/Nmixx "Nmixx") was announced for a February 22 debut, with their debut single album, *[Ad Mare](/wiki/Ad_Mare "Ad Mare")*.[[92]](#cite_note-92) After Twice's success in the U.S., JYP Entertainment expanded their partnership with [Republic Records](/wiki/Republic_Records "Republic Records") in February, by signing both Stray Kids and Itzy under Republic Records for promotions.[[93]](#cite_note-93) In April, the market cap of JYP Entertainment had risen from 1.33 trillion KRW in the previous year to 2.24 trillion KRW, an increase of 1 trillion KRW in the first three months of 2022. The company's stock prices soared to 66,200 KRW on April 8, surpassing company's record.[[94]](#cite_note-94) On July 12, all nine members of Twice renewed their contracts with the company.[[95]](#cite_note-95) On September 26, all members of Day6 renewed their contracts with the company.[[96]](#cite_note-96) In December, [Jinni](/wiki/Jini_(singer) "Jini (singer)") both left the company and the group Nmixx, due to personal reasons.[[97]](#cite_note-Jinni-97)

In 2023, the competition show *[A2K](/wiki/A2K_(TV_program) "A2K (TV program)")* and the second season of *[Nizi Project](/wiki/Nizi_Project_season_2 "Nizi Project season 2")* both aired. *A2K* led to the formation of the group [Vcha](/wiki/Girlset "Girlset"), a joint venture between JYP Entertainment and Republic Records.[[98]](#cite_note-Vcha-98) The second season of *Nizi Project* concluded with the line up for the boy group [Nexz](/wiki/Nexz "Nexz"), a joint venture with Sony Records Japan.[[99]](#cite_note-99) Both groups released their debut single in 2024.[[100]](#cite_note-100)[[101]](#cite_note-101) In August 2024, Innit Entertainment was established – the company's management subsidiary for actors and artists.[[102]](#cite_note-Innit-102)

In 2025, the company's newest boy groups [KickFlip](/wiki/KickFlip "KickFlip") and CIIU were launched.[[103]](#cite_note-103)[[104]](#cite_note-CIIU-104) The girl group Vcha was rebranded as Girlset in August without original members KG and Kaylee, both of whom left JYP Entertainment.[[105]](#cite_note-Girlset-105) By September, all five members of the girl group [Itzy](/wiki/Itzy "Itzy") renewed their contact with the company.[[106]](#cite_note-106)

## Joint ventures

JYP Entertainment's records are distributed worldwide by [The Orchard](/wiki/The_Orchard_(company) "The Orchard (company)") since March 2019.[[107]](#cite_note-107)

### KMP Holdings and KT Music

In March 2010, [KMP Holdings](/wiki/KMP_Holdings "KMP Holdings") was established via a [joint venture](/wiki/Joint_venture "Joint venture") between JYP Entertainment, [SM Entertainment](/wiki/SM_Entertainment "SM Entertainment"), [YG Entertainment](/wiki/YG_Entertainment "YG Entertainment"), Star Empire, Media Line, CAN Entertainment and Music Factory Entertainment. KMP Holdings was acquired by [KT Music](/wiki/Genie_Music "Genie Music") in November 2012. In June 2013, KT Music absorbed KMP's distribution network. In January 2014, the seven talent agencies behind [KMP Holdings](/wiki/KMP_Holdings "KMP Holdings") formed a collective bond partnership and bought 13.48% of [KT Music](/wiki/KT_Music "KT Music")'s stocks, leaving [KT Corporation](/wiki/KT_Corporation "KT Corporation") with 49.99%.[[44]](#cite_note-gaonchart1-44)

### United Asia Management

In 2011, JYP Entertainment joined forces with SM Entertainment, YG Entertainment, [KeyEast](/wiki/KeyEast "KeyEast"), AMENT and Star J Entertainment to form United Asia Management in an effort to promote Korean pop music internationally.[[108]](#cite_note-UAM-108)

### FLO

On January 31, 2018, [iRiver](/wiki/IRiver "IRiver") announced its entry into the South Korean music industry. Together with parent company [SK Telecom](/wiki/SK_Telecom "SK Telecom") and music labels SM Entertainment, JYP Entertainment and [Big Hit Entertainment](/wiki/Big_Hit_Entertainment "Big Hit Entertainment"), the company launched a new online music store, FLO, in the second half of 2018.[[109]](#cite_note-109)

### Beijing Shinsung Entertainment

On April 5, 2017, Ocean Music and JYP Entertainment jointly established the Beijing Xin Sheng Entertainment Co., Ltd. for indoor recreational facilities operation, organization of cultural and artistic exchanges, film and television planning, and other aspects of cooperation. A few months later, [Park Jin-young](/wiki/J._Y._Park "J. Y. Park"), [Jackson Wang](/wiki/Jackson_Wang "Jackson Wang"), [Fei](/wiki/Fei_(singer) "Fei (singer)") and a 10-year-old JYP Chinese trainee went to China to record a roadshow-style audition show to recruit more trainees with the goal of creating a hip-hop oriented Chinese boy group. The name of the show was *Guaishushu Is Coming*, and the concept was to travel across different cities with large-scale auditions and then have a final round to select the members who will be trained in South Korea.[[60]](#cite_note-qdaily.com-60)

### NCC Entertainment (NCC Station)

NCC Entertainment is a jointly produced management team by Tencent Music Corporation and JYP Beijing Cultural Exchange Ltd located in Beijing, China.[[60]](#cite_note-qdaily.com-60) It is working to promote its Chinese artists more, despite the ban placed on Korean entertainment and to further promote the Chinese boy group, [Boy Story](/wiki/Boy_Story "Boy Story") in China.[[110]](#cite_note-110)

## Philanthropy

During the [COVID-19 pandemic](/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic"), JYP Entertainment donated US$410 thousand to the Community Chest of South Korea on February 28, 2020.[[122]](#cite_note-123) On March 8, 2022, the company made a donation [₩](/wiki/South_Korean_won "South Korean won")300 million to the Hope Bridge Disaster Relief Association, to help the victims of the massive wildfire that started in Uljin, Gyeongbuk which had spread to Samcheok, Gangwon.[[123]](#cite_note-124) On February 12, 2023, the company donated ₩500 million through [World Vision International](/wiki/World_Vision_International "World Vision International"), to help the aftermath of the [2023 Turkey–Syria earthquakes](/wiki/2023_Turkey%E2%80%93Syria_earthquakes "2023 Turkey–Syria earthquakes").[[124]](#cite_note-125)

### Trending on Billboard

K-pop visionary [J.Y. Park](https://www.billboard.com/artist/j-y-park/) is making the leap into politics.

South Korea’s President Lee Jae Myung has appointed Park (Park Jin-young), CEO of JYP Entertainment, as co-chair of the Presidential Committee on Popular Culture Exchange.

Announced Tuesday, Sept. 9, the new presidential committee has a mission [to promote South Korean culture abroad](https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/east-asia/founder-of-k-pop-powerhouse-jyp-appointed-to-ministerial-level-post-on-pop-culture) while expanding exposure to international pop culture domestically.

Park shared his thoughts with his 2 million Instagram followers. “I thought long and hard about taking on a government role, as it felt burdensome and worrisome in many ways for someone from the entertainment industry. But with K-pop facing such a special opportunity right now,” he added, “I decided to embrace it and make the most of it.”

### Related

### [Just in Time For Valentine's Day, Spotify Shares Which Love-Themed Lyrics From Taylor Swift, Djo and HUNTR/X Are Most Shared](https://www.billboard.com/business/streaming/spotify-most-shared-love-themed-lyrics-swift-upgrades-1236172491/)

* [Gil Kaufman](https://www.billboard.com/author/gil-kaufman/)

Widely loved by the public, Park debuted as a solo artist in 1994, and last year presented a solo concert in Seoul to celebrate 30 years in showbiz.

After founding JYP Entertainment in 1996, he launched artists including Rain, Wonder Girls, 2PM, TWICE, Day6 and Stray Kids, elevating the company to one of Korea’s top entertainment agencies.

In 2009, at the height of the Wonder Girls’ domestic popularity, he moved to the United States and essentially started from scratch. He secured the group a spot as the opening act for the Jonas Brothers’ North American tour, and in that year guided the English-language release of the [Wonder Girls](https://www.billboard.com/artist/wonder-girls/)’ “Nobody,” which became the [first Korean song](https://www.billboard.com/music/music-news/wonder-girls-nobody-10-year-anniversary-k-pop-hot-100-chart-8476481/) to impact the Billboard Hot 100, debuting and peaking at No. 76, for what turned out to be a week-long stay on the chart.

Park also posted a photo of the Wonder Girls from 2009 on his Instagram, remarking: “My dream remains the same as it was in 2003 when I went to the U.S. to promote Korean artists to American record labels, in 2009 when the Wonder Girls became the first Korean act to enter the Billboard Hot 100 chart, and now: for K-pop to be loved worldwide.”

He promises to “work hard so that junior artists can get a lot of better opportunities. And K-pop will take a step further and promote our culture. We will do our best to make it a platform for people around the world to understand and communicate with each other.”

Park isn’t the first entertainer to enter politics in Korea. Yoo In-chon — a widely beloved actor from the 1980s through the 1990s — served twice as Minister of Culture, Sports and Tourism. It is unprecedented, however, for someone who remains an active artist to be appointed to a minister-level position.

Meanwhile, shares of JYP Entertainment — for which Park is the largest shareholder — were up 4.93% from the previous day as of 9 a.m. KST, and are currently trading 2.8% higher.

The company’s outlook itself also appears solid, thanks to the ongoing success of its frontline acts. Among them, TWICE, which is celebrating its 10th anniversary this year, and is currently on the road for their fourth worldwide concert tour.

Stray Kids recently set a new K-pop record as *Karma* became their seventh consecutive No. 1 on the Billboard 200, beginning with *[ODDINARY](https://www.billboard.com/music/chart-beat/stray-kids-karma-seventh-number-one-album-billboard-200-1236055754/)* in 2022 (all debuted at the top spot). Also, Park has introduced localized idol groups through the affiliates of JYP Japan, JYP China, and JYP America.

## 2. characteristic

It currently owns 15.67% of JYP Entertainment's stock, which is worth 700 billion won based on the market price in the stock market in July 2023. Park Jin-young was the CEO of JYP Entertainment in the past, but she is not now. However, she is in a position of legal responsibility in management as an in-house registered director and is still in charge of artists, production, and sales as a representative producer at the head office. She is in charge of making final decisions, especially when it comes to launching new artists within the company.  
  
His English stage name is JY Park or JYP, the initials of Jinyoung Park, and as a producer he uses the pen name JY Park "The Asiansoul."

## [18.](#toc) interview

> A. In fact, it is good to become a Cheongchuleoram. You have to work harder to do that. It's actually not good when you hear that. It's because I've spent a lot of my life teaching and raising other idols.
>
> ---
>
> Q. As expected, JYP's best artist is Park Jin-young?

> A. There is something I decided 3 years ago. As for the life of a singer, let’s dance and sing when we are 60 years old. Also, when I looked at the company at that time, the companies competing for first and second place did not exceed 1 trillion in market capitalization. What should I do to get over 1 trillion? Sales and operating profit simulations were also conducted. As a result, it was concluded that the current state could not be overcome. The only thing I gained from being in the US was that I knew everything about the structure of American record labels. I learned how mass production systems such as Universal, Sony Music, and Warner are possible. After that, I decided to create a company without Park Jin-young. At first, I was terribly perplexed. Originally, I decided everything, but since I didn't, a music video or a nonsensical result came out. After three years of trial and error, the system is finally settling in. I also tried singing by external composers, and in the meantime, I raised more than 30 composers. I focused on minimizing my influence. It took 3 years for that to become a good result. The system was almost right.
>
> ---
>
> Q. Recently, the JYP system is moving away from Park Jin-young and becoming more open.

> A. We are a company with a system that always releases if there is no chance. They export a lot compared to other companies. There are several reasons. The musical direction doesn't match, or the lifestyle doesn't match. So always be ready to go out. If your grades fall below halfway, you won't be able to practice. The lives of my trainee friends are also important, so I make them ready to go back. If you don't have the confidence to debut, send them out immediately. All of them are someone's precious sons and daughters, but I can't hold them. If not, prepare to export right away.
>
> ---
>
> Q. There are many singers who were JYP trainees in the music industry.

> A. First of all, the goal is to create 10 labels. They went through trial and error with labels such as AQE and Big Hit. It is still difficult to make a label as an idol. It seemed like there would be a chance of winning if we made a musician-oriented label. That's why I made 'Studio J' and put in G-Soul and 15+. G-Soul had a good debut, and Fifteen End had good returns. In this way, we are developing the know-how to operate more than 10 labels. I want to build a company that will thrive even if I die. After Steve Jobs died and the stock price fell in half, I thought I had to somehow create a company without me. When we compete for 1st or 2nd place, we can’t do that experiment, but since we fall behind, we can do anything.
>
> ---
>
> Q. Do you have any future goals? ( **Interview with TenAsia in 2015** )

> A. Business is only fun when you dream. The only meetings I attend are A&R meetings. It's a creative group, but I'm only 1/15 of its members. I spent a long time figuring out how to select 14 other people besides me. And you can think of management as having a two-hour conversation with the company president every Saturday at 2:00 PM. Standing on stage is the end of physical pleasure. Business is sane, and the stage is a hallucination.
>
> ---
>
> Q. You said that you hate management and that you like being on stage the most. Do you feel really good when you talk about this? ( **Interview with the JoongAng Ilbo in 2015** )

> A. When I look at my friends, I see health as the best value, but no matter how well I sing or how well I dance, I can't do it unless I'm bright, clear, and healthy. I don't know why I have to make my friends' dreams come true. Making money is important, but I like being happy with the process. If one of the skills and character is lacking, I help them coexist as much as possible, and my dream is to see friends who have both.
>
> ---
>
> Q. Is there anything you want from the singers under your agency?

> A. I respect you the most. Next is Bo-won Nam, Nam-bong Baek, and Moon-sik Yoon. 10 years ago, I went to see Ms. Gong's performance, and I sang and acted for two hours, then moved freely, and wow, I thought this was a clown. I too want to be a clown.
>
> ---
>
> Q. You said that you respect Ms. [Gong Ok-](/w/%EA%B3%B5%EC%98%A5%EC%A7%84 "Gong Okjin") jin, is that so?

> A. I am not called the boss or representative. My official title at the company is Jinyoung Park. There is a great fear of moving up. It's not so much that I'm afraid of being lonely, but rather that I'm afraid that I won't be able to act like a clown, that I'll lose my ability to make others cry or make them laugh.
>
> ---
>
> Q. It is not easy to take the representative of a company lightly.

> A. When I am a producer, the people next to me collapse. It's fussy, two nights a day, so. Also, I'm definitely a sucker, but I also like to study. These days, I study one day a week differently. The world and humans want to know who made it and why. In conclusion, he seems like a fun person. It's fun to be serious and stupid at the same time.
>
> ---
>

Park Jin-young (Korean: 박진영; born December 13, 1971), also known by his stage names J. Y. Park and The Asiansoul or the initials JYP, is a South Korean singer-songwriter, record producer, record executive, and reality television show judge. Park rose to stardom as a singer following the release of his 1994 debut album, Blue City. In 1997, he became the founder of JYP Entertainment, one of the most profitable entertainment agencies in South Korea.

As the head of JYP Entertainment from 1997 to 2011, Park has developed and managed successful K-pop artists including 2PM, Day6, Got7, Itzy, KickFlip, Miss A, Nmixx, Rain "Rain (entertainer)"), Stray Kids, Twice, Xdinary Heroes and Wonder Girls, as well as Mandopop group Boy Story and J-pop groups Nexz and NiziU.

**Park Jin-young** ([Korean](/wiki/Korean_language "Korean language"): 박진영; born December 13, 1971),[[1]](#cite_note-birth_date-1)[[A]](#cite_note-dob-2) also known by his stage names **J. Y. Park** and **The Asiansoul** or the initials **JYP**, is a South Korean singer-songwriter, record producer, record executive, and reality television show judge.[[3]](#cite_note-4)[[4]](#cite_note-5) Park rose to stardom as a singer following the release of his 1994 debut album, *Blue City*.[[5]](#cite_note-6) In 1997, he became the founder of [JYP Entertainment](/wiki/JYP_Entertainment "JYP Entertainment"), one of the most profitable entertainment agencies in South Korea.[[6]](#cite_note-7)

As the head of JYP Entertainment from 1997 to 2011, Park has developed and managed successful [K-pop](/wiki/K-pop "K-pop") artists including [2PM](/wiki/2PM "2PM"), [Day6](/wiki/Day6 "Day6"), [Got7](/wiki/Got7 "Got7"), [Itzy](/wiki/Itzy "Itzy"), [KickFlip](/wiki/KickFlip "KickFlip"), [Miss A](/wiki/Miss_A "Miss A"), [Nmixx](/wiki/Nmixx "Nmixx"), [Rain](/wiki/Rain_(entertainer) "Rain (entertainer)"), [Stray Kids](/wiki/Stray_Kids "Stray Kids"), [Twice](/wiki/Twice "Twice"), [Xdinary Heroes](/wiki/Xdinary_Heroes "Xdinary Heroes") and [Wonder Girls](/wiki/Wonder_Girls "Wonder Girls"), as well as [Mandopop](/wiki/Mandopop "Mandopop") group [Boy Story](/wiki/Boy_Story "Boy Story") and [J-pop](/wiki/J-pop "J-pop") groups [Nexz](/wiki/Nexz "Nexz") and [NiziU](/wiki/NiziU "NiziU").[[7]](#cite_note-8)[[8]](#cite_note-9)[[9]](#cite_note-10)

## Early life and education

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=J.Y._Park&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")]

Park was born in [Gwangjin District](/wiki/Gwangjin_District "Gwangjin District"), [Seoul](/wiki/Seoul "Seoul"), South Korea.[[2]](#cite_note-JYP-3) His father was a news correspondent based in the U.S. At age 9, Park moved with his mother to New York following his father's reassignment. They lived there for three years before Park returned to Seoul for high school. He later attended [Yonsei University](/wiki/Yonsei_University "Yonsei University"), during which time he released his first two albums. He graduated with a bachelor's in [geology](/wiki/Geology "Geology") in 1996.[[10]](#cite_note-11) He has an older sister.[[11]](#cite_note-:1-12) Park learned music composition and production for two years from [Kim Hyung-suk](/wiki/Kim_Hyeong-seok "Kim Hyeong-seok"), who is considered one of the best pop music composers and producers of all time in South Korea.[[12]](#cite_note-13)

## Career

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=J.Y._Park&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

Park originally debuted as the trio boy group "Park Jin Young and the NG (New Generation)" (박진영과 신세대), with [Kim Soo-chul](/wiki/Kim_Soo-chul "Kim Soo-chul") as a producer, and members Cho Hye-sung and Yoon Tae-jin. Their first album 'Floating time' (떠도는 시간) was not successful.[[13]](#cite_note-14)[[14]](#cite_note-15)[[15]](#cite_note-16)[[16]](#cite_note-17) Park's notability within the Korean music industry began in 1994 when he debuted as a solo artist with the song "Don't Leave Me" (날 떠나지마) from his debut album *Blue City*.[[17]](#cite_note-18) During this period, he met composer and long-time collaborator [Bang Si-hyuk](/wiki/Bang_Si-hyuk "Bang Si-hyuk"). In 1997, Park founded his label and agency [JYP Entertainment](/wiki/JYP_Entertainment "JYP Entertainment"), then known as Tae-Hong Planning Corp (대홍기획). That same year, he was tasked by EBM (now [SidusHQ](/wiki/SidusHQ "SidusHQ")) with preparing the members of its project group for debut; the five-member act was eventually called [g.o.d](/wiki/G.o.d "G.o.d") and debuted two years later.[[18]](#cite_note-MBC2014-19) The success of g.o.d as one of the country's most popular and bestselling groups of the early 2000s would further establish Bang and Park's reputation as hit makers.[[19]](#cite_note-20)[[20]](#cite_note-21)[[21]](#cite_note-22)

In 2004, Park ventured into the American music industry, becoming the first Asian producer to cross over to the U.S., producing music for [Will Smith](/wiki/Will_Smith "Will Smith"), [Mase](/wiki/Mase "Mase") and [Cassie](/wiki/Cassie_(singer) "Cassie (singer)").[[22]](#cite_note-auto-23)[*[unreliable source?](/wiki/Wikipedia:Reliable_sources "Wikipedia:Reliable sources")*][[23]](#cite_note-24)

In May 2008, Park collaborated with [Jackie Chan](/wiki/Jackie_Chan "Jackie Chan") to form the I Love Asia Project, prompted by the [earthquake tragedy in China](/wiki/2008_Sichuan_earthquake "2008 Sichuan earthquake"). Park produced the song "Smile Again" along with Chan and Korean director [Kang Je-gyu](/wiki/Kang_Je-gyu "Kang Je-gyu") to raise funds for relief efforts in [Sichuan](/wiki/Sichuan "Sichuan").[[24]](#cite_note-25) The song featured an array of Korean talents including actors and singers as well as [figure skater](/wiki/Figure_skating "Figure skating") [Kim Yuna](/wiki/Kim_Yuna "Kim Yuna").[[25]](#cite_note-26) The music video was released on JYP Entertainment's YouTube channel on June 30.[[26]](#cite_note-27)

In October 2009, Park became the first Korean songwriter, together with [RAINSTONE](/wiki/Rainstone "Rainstone"), to reach the [Billboard Hot 100 Chart](/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") with the [Wonder Girls](/wiki/Wonder_Girls "Wonder Girls") hit "[Nobody](/wiki/Nobody_(Wonder_Girls_song) "Nobody (Wonder Girls song)")" which debuted at No. 76.[[27]](#cite_note-28)

On December 3, 2009, Park released his single "No Love No More".[[28]](#cite_note-29) On April 22, 2011, Park collaborated with [Brown Eyed Girls](/wiki/Brown_Eyed_Girls "Brown Eyed Girls")' [Ga-In](/wiki/Gain_(singer) "Gain (singer)"), releasing the duet track "Someone Else". The song charted at No. 2 on the [*Gaon* Digital Chart](/wiki/Gaon_Digital_Chart "Gaon Digital Chart") and sold over a million copies. This was his first release in about two years. Park followed up his success with "Someone Else" by releasing the single "You're the One" on April 28, 2012. The song rose to No. 3 and sold over 1.5 million copies.

In 2015, Park released the song "Who's Your Mama?" featuring [Lucky J](/wiki/Lucky_J "Lucky J")'s [Jessi](/wiki/Jessi_(musician) "Jessi (musician)"). The song became a hit, displacing fellow label-mates [Miss A](/wiki/Miss_A "Miss A") from first spot on the Korean charts.[[29]](#cite_note-30)[*[full citation needed](/wiki/Wikipedia:Citing_sources#What_information_to_include "Wikipedia:Citing sources")*] Later that year, he participated in the [*Infinite Challenge Yeongdong Expressway Music Festival*](/wiki/Infinite_Challenge#Infinite_Challenge_Music_Festival "Infinite Challenge"), forming the duo Dancing Genome with comedian [Yoo Jae-suk](/wiki/Yoo_Jae-suk "Yoo Jae-suk") and releasing the song "I'm So Sexy".[[30]](#cite_note-auto1-31)

In 2016, Park released a single titled 'Still Alive'.[[30]](#cite_note-auto1-31) During the same period, he appeared in the [Conan O'Brien](/wiki/Conan_O%27Brien "Conan O'Brien") special '*Conan in Korea*', recording a song with Conan O'Brien, [Steven Yeun](/wiki/Steven_Yeun "Steven Yeun") & [Park Ji-min](/wiki/Park_Ji-min_(singer,_born_1997) "Park Ji-min (singer, born 1997)") titled 'Fire', with label-mates [Wonder Girls](/wiki/Wonder_Girls "Wonder Girls") and [Twice](/wiki/Twice "Twice") appearing in the music video.[[31]](#cite_note-32) The song was released on Conan O'Brien's YouTube channel on April 9.[[32]](#cite_note-33) Park also appeared in the Korean variety show *[Sister's Slam Dunk](/wiki/Sister%27s_Slam_Dunk "Sister's Slam Dunk")* in 2016, producing the cast's single titled '[Shut Up](/wiki/Shut_Up_(Unnies_song) "Shut Up (Unnies song)")'.[[33]](#cite_note-34) The song unexpectedly achieved a real-time chart all-kill upon release.[[34]](#cite_note-35)[*[unreliable source?](/wiki/Wikipedia:Reliable_sources "Wikipedia:Reliable sources")*] On September 22, 2016, it was reported that Park would be producing the title track of girl-group [I.O.I](/wiki/I.O.I "I.O.I") for their final album prior to disbandment.[[35]](#cite_note-36)[*[full citation needed](/wiki/Wikipedia:Citing_sources#What_information_to_include "Wikipedia:Citing sources")*] The song, titled "[Very Very Very](/wiki/Very_Very_Very "Very Very Very")" was released on October 16, 2016.[*[citation needed](/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*] It achieved commercial success upon release, earning a perfect all-kill on the Korean charts and topping the [*Gaon* Digital Chart](/wiki/Gaon_Digital_Chart "Gaon Digital Chart").[[36]](#cite_note-37)[*[unreliable source?](/wiki/Wikipedia:Reliable_sources "Wikipedia:Reliable sources")*][[37]](#cite_note-38) In 2019, Park released a song titled 'Fever' featured by Superbee and [BIBI](/wiki/Bibi_(singer) "Bibi (singer)").

On August 11, 2020, Park released his autobiography, *Live for What?*[[38]](#cite_note-JY_Park_Story-39) One day later, Park released a new single, "[When We Disco](/wiki/When_We_Disco "When We Disco")", which was a duet with [Sunmi](/wiki/Sunmi "Sunmi"). This was his first collaboration with Sunmi since her departure from JYP Entertainment and the [Wonder Girls](/wiki/Wonder_Girls "Wonder Girls").[[39]](#cite_note-40) The single peaked at #3 at the [Gaon Digital Chart](/wiki/Gaon_Digital_Chart "Gaon Digital Chart"), becoming his sixth Top 10 song in the chart.[[40]](#cite_note-41)

On April 26, 2021, it was reported that Park and [Psy](/wiki/Psy "Psy"), the founder of [P Nation](/wiki/P_Nation "P Nation"), will collaborate to form a new boy group each in *[Loud](/wiki/Loud_(South_Korean_TV_series) "Loud (South Korean TV series)")*, which premiered on June 5, 2021 on [SBS](/wiki/Seoul_Broadcasting_System "Seoul Broadcasting System").[[41]](#cite_note-42)

In November 2022, Park released the single "Groove Back", which was released on November 21, but the music video was released three days prior, according to the agency.[[42]](#cite_note-43) later Park confirmed to hold a solo concert, In Japan for the first time in 7 years at Yokohama [Pia Arena MM](/wiki/Pia_Arena_MM "Pia Arena MM"), January 28–29, 2023.[[43]](#cite_note-44) On September 16, 2024, a television special *The KBS Grand Project — 30th Anniversary Special Entertainer JYP* aired on [KBS2](/wiki/KBS2 "KBS2"). Celebrating the 30th anniversary of Park's debut, it featured appearances from g.o.d, Rain, Sunye, Sunmi, 2PM and [Twice](/wiki/Twice "Twice").[[44]](#cite_note-45)

Park Jin-young is celebrating his 30th debut anniversary with a solo concert, Still JYP. The concert, scheduled for December 27 to 29 at Olympic Hall in Seoul, features his greatest hits and is designed to appeal to fans of all ages. Additional tickets are available for purchase through Interpark, YES24, and Naver Reservations. Park Jin-young's legacy continues to thrive, with international performances planned.[[45]](#cite_note-46)

On September 9, 2025, Park Jin-young was appointed as the co-chairman (minister level) of the Popular Culture Exchange Committee directly under the president, [Lee Jae Myung](/wiki/Lee_Jae_Myung "Lee Jae Myung").[[46]](#cite_note-47)

### Acting

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=J.Y._Park&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Acting")]

In early 2011, JYP made his acting debut in *[Dream High](/wiki/Dream_High "Dream High")*, for which he received a nomination for New Actor of the Year at the [Baeksang Arts Awards](/wiki/Baeksang_Arts_Awards "Baeksang Arts Awards"). In January 2012 he was seen in the sequel to Dream High called *[Dream High 2](/wiki/Dream_High_2 "Dream High 2")*.[[47]](#cite_note-48)[*[unreliable source?](/wiki/Wikipedia:Reliable_sources "Wikipedia:Reliable sources")*]

In 2011, Park made his film debut as Choi Young In, a man on a mission to hand-deliver 5 million dollars, in *Five Million Dollar Man* with [Jo Sung-ha](/wiki/Jo_Sung-ha "Jo Sung-ha") and [Min Hyo-rin](/wiki/Min_Hyo-rin "Min Hyo-rin").[[48]](#cite_note-49) The film was released on July 19, 2012.[[49]](#cite_note-50)[*[unreliable source?](/wiki/Wikipedia:Reliable_sources "Wikipedia:Reliable sources")*]

## Personal life

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=J.Y._Park&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Personal life")]

### Relationships

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=J.Y._Park&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Relationships")]

In 1999, Park Jin-young married Seo Yoon-jeong. In March 2009, the couple announced their divorce.[[50]](#cite_note-51) On October 10, 2013, he married a woman nine years younger than him.[[51]](#cite_note-JYP_tried_to_sell_agency-52) On January 25, 2019, his daughter was born, and Park wrote "*This Small Hand*" for her and his father, with a documentary-style music video released on February 9.[[11]](#cite_note-:1-12) In the music video, it was revealed that his father was in the late stage of [Alzheimer's disease](/wiki/Alzheimer%27s_disease "Alzheimer's disease") and could no longer recognize him. All proceeds from the song went to the Green Umbrella Foundation ([ChildFund](/wiki/ChildFund "ChildFund") Korea) to help children in need.[[52]](#cite_note-53)

### Religion

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=J.Y._Park&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Religion")]

Park is a born-again Christian and leads weekly Bible practices.[[38]](#cite_note-JY_Park_Story-39) Park turned to several faiths to fill the "void in [his] heart" after his divorce before finding his faith in Christianity.[[38]](#cite_note-JY_Park_Story-39)

### Plagiarism allegation

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=J.Y._Park&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Plagiarism allegation")]

On February 10, 2011, songwriter Kim Sin-il filed a lawsuit against Park claiming that "Someday", sung by [IU](/wiki/IU_(entertainer) "IU (entertainer)") and composed by Park, plagiarized Kim's song "To My Man". Kim alleged that the beginnings of the two songs, including the jazz chords, are almost identical and sued Park for 110 million won.[[53]](#cite_note-54) Park denied the allegations, and no settlement was reached after several court hearings.[[54]](#cite_note-55) On February 10, 2012, the Seoul Central District Court ruled that "Someday" was plagiarized from Kim's song, and ordered Park to pay 21.67 million won in damages to Kim.[[55]](#cite_note-56) Park appealed the ruling, but on January 24, 2013, the Seoul High Court ruled against Park and ordered him to pay 56.93 million won to Kim.[[56]](#cite_note-57) In 2015, the Supreme Court overturned the previous rulings in light of new evidence demonstrating that the melody and chord progressions were very common, specifically citing [Kirk Franklin](/wiki/Kirk_Franklin "Kirk Franklin")'s 2002 song "[Hosanna](/wiki/The_Rebirth_of_Kirk_Franklin "The Rebirth of Kirk Franklin")".[[57]](#cite_note-58)

## Philanthropy

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=J.Y._Park&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Philanthropy")]

In December 2022, Park donated 500 million won each to Samsung Seoul Hospital and World Vision, an international relief and development non-governmental organization.[[58]](#cite_note-59) In December 2023, he donated 200 million won each to 5 hospitals in South Korea to support the treatment of underprivileged children.[[59]](#cite_note-60)

title: CJ ENM CEO Reveals 2026 Global Expansion Plans
content:
Global Expansion Beyond Content Sales

The company has already begun positioning for potential market access. In early February 2026, CJ ENM announced ONECEAD, a joint venture with JYP CHINA and Tencent Music Entertainment focused on artist development and management in Greater China. The partnership builds on CJ ENM’s success with LAPONE Entertainment in Japan, which established artists like JO1 and INI. Despite ongoing restrictions, the Greater China market (including Hong Kong and Taiwan) represented K-pop's second-largest export market in 2023 at $319.58 million.

The company also established CJ ENM Middle East LLC in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia in 2025, a market with no existing Korean diaspora infrastructure to build upon. [...] CJ ENM CEO Reveals 2026 Global Expansion Plans

"Our strategy is to continue growing the subscriber base of our digital platforms, like TVING and Mnet Plus," he said. "By strengthening those platforms and expanding our recurring revenue, we aim to gradually increase our content investment over time."

TVING’s long-discussed merger with rival platform Wavve, which would create South Korea’s largest domestic streaming service, remains in progress with no clear timeline.

CEO Yoon Sang Hyun of Korean entertainment conglomerate CJ ENM

cj enm

CJ ENM, the South Korean entertainment conglomerate behind Studio Dragon and streaming platform TVING, is fundamentally rethinking how it develops content. CEO Yoon Sang-hyun, who took the helm in 2023, is steering the company away from short-term content sales toward long-term IP value maximization, which is a shift that could reshape how Korean studios approach transmedia expansion.

"2026 will be a year where we focus more firmly on increasing the long-term value of the IP we create," Yoon told me through a translator, speaking just days after the company reported fourth-quarter 2025 results that saw operating profit more than double year-over-year despite declining revenue.

The shift represents a strategic recalibration for the company behind _Parasite_, _Queen of Tears_, and K-pop infrastructure like KCON and MAMA. Rather than treating each drama or film as a discrete transaction, CJ ENM is now structuring deals to capture transmedia revenue — musicals, merchandise, character licensing — from the earliest development stages.

PROMOTED

"We're not focusing on selling content as a single item and then making revenue from there," Yoon explained. "We're going much deeper, expanding to various forms of transmedia, including musicals and films, and further leveraging IP through merchandise, commerce, character licensing, and any other secondary business that can come after the content we make."

The IP Value Thesis
-------------------

The strategic pivot stems from lessons learned on projects like _Bugonia_, CJ ENM’s first Hollywood production as direct producer rather than financier. The Yorgos Lanthimos-directed film, a remake of Korean IP _Save the Green Planet_ starring Emma Stone and Jesse Plemons, earned a Best Picture nomination at this year’s upcoming Oscars.

CJ ENM’s Hollywood ambitions faced mixed results this awards season. While _Bugonia_ secured its Best Picture nomination, Yoon personally was hoping for more recognition for Park Chan-wook’s _No Other Choice,_ which was shut out entirely. "It’s a shame. It’s disappointing that we did not receive nominations," Yoon acknowledged, with a disclaimer that it was his own opinion and not the company’s, "but if _Bugonia_ ultimately wins, we would consider it a great honour."

The contrasting fates underscore the unpredictability of prestige filmmaking, but Yoon frames both films as learning experiences. "With _Bugonia_, we were able to be involved from the very earliest stages of development and producing, which gave us the opportunity to rethink how our IP could be developed and positioned for a global audience," Yoon said. The experience, he added, became "a valuable learning experience" that's now informing the company's broader IP strategy.

The approach extends to international partnerships. CJ ENM’s three-year deal with Japan’s TBS, for instance, goes beyond simple format switches and sales. Their Japanese adaptation of _Marry My Husband,_ which became the most-watched Amazon Original drama in Japan upon release, was "very locally tailored" and "built around re-imagining IP from the very early beginning of the development stages," according to Yoon.

The Korean Film Problem
-----------------------

While CJ ENM expands globally, Yoon pointed to a persistent challenge closer to home: the promise of _Parasite_'s historic Oscar win has yet to fully materialize for Korea's theatrical industry.

"A lot of key content creators say the entertainment industry in Korea divides between before _Parasite_ and after _Parasite_," Yoon explained. "That's how powerful _Parasite_ was." Following the film's Best Picture win in 2020, global producers and platforms became far more eager to collaborate with Korean creators, accelerating the international expansion of Korean content.

But the pandemic arrived shortly after, derailing that momentum. Korea’s theatrical market has recovered to only 60-70% of pre-pandemic levels, Yoon told me, unlike markets such as the United States, India, and China, which have seen greater recovery (albeit in keeping with generally slumping numbers of theater-goers).

"Korean audiences, compared to any other audiences in the world, are very trendy. They're extremely sensitive to changes," Yoon explained. The shift to streaming has fundamentally altered viewing habits, leaving Korean film producers "continuously questioning what kinds of films should we make now."

CJ ENM's answer diverges sharply from Hollywood's tentpole strategy. Rather than massive-budget productions, the company is focusing on "mid to lower budget films that are more grounded in authentic storytelling and emotional sincerity."

"Unlike Hollywood, it is particularly difficult for us to predict trends far in advance," Yoon said. "That makes it very challenging to commit to massive big budget productions from the development stage."

The strategy prioritizes rebuilding "a healthy investment cycle within the industry first" by discovering "young creators with untold original stories and developing projects that aim for high creative impact with very efficient production scales."

It’s a notable shift for the company behind _Parasite_, which cost $15.5 million and grossed $263 million globally before winning four Oscars including Best Picture. But Yoon’s caution reflects the broader struggles of Korean cinema post-pandemic, and CJ ENM's determination to avoid overextending on projects that may not recoup in a diminished theatrical market.

The Numbers Behind the Strategy
-------------------------------

The cautious approach to Korean theatrical is reflected in CJ ENM’s latest financial results, which show a company navigating both opportunity and constraint.

CJ ENM’s [fourth-quarter 2025 earnings](https://www.cjenm.com/en/investors/ir/earnings-release/), reported in early February, illustrate both the company’s challenges and concurrent persistence. While overall revenue declined year-over-year, operating profit more than doubled, driven by strong performance across key divisions:

Studio Dragon, the drama production powerhouse, posted operating profit of 30.4 billion Korean won for full-year 2025, with fourth-quarter revenue of 145.9 billion won and a 12.7% operating margin. The company’s hit series _Bon Appétit, Your Majesty_[ranked third globally on Netflix](https://www.cjenm.com/en/news/studio-dragons-bon-app%C3%A9tit-your-majesty-ranks-no-3-globally-by-hours-viewed-on-netflix-h2-2025/) by hours viewed in the second half of 2025, accumulating 588.3 million hours, trailing only _Wednesday Season 2_ and _Stranger Things 5_.

Fifth Season, the Los Angeles-based studio CJ ENM acquired an 80% stake in for $785 million in January 2022, reported fourth-quarter revenue of 184 billion won and operating profit of 10 billion won. The studio's _Severance_ Season 2 won eight Emmy Awards and drew record viewership on Apple TV+, marking what Yoon called "a turning point" after restructuring and layoffs in 2024.

TVING, CJ ENM’s streaming platform, posted fourth-quarter revenue of 118.8 billion won with an operating loss of 4.1 billion won, which was an improvement from previous quarters. The platform ended 2024 with 5.2 million subscribers and captured 34% of South Korea's premium video-on-demand viewership, up from 24% in the first half of 2024.

Mnet Plus, the company's K-pop content platform, reached 44 million cumulative users by late 2025 with peak monthly active users of 20 million. "In 2026 we will be able to double the current revenue level," Yoon projected, noting the platform plans to quadruple content investment this year.

Rights Strategy: The Critical Shift
-----------------------------------

Perhaps the most operationally significant change involves how CJ ENM structures deals with creators from the outset.

"Before, we tended to evaluate scripts primarily through the lens of immediate hit potential, how successful it might be as a single piece of content," Yoon explained. "Going forward, we’re expanding that perspective. In addition to commercial potential, we now ask: How expandable is this IP? Can it evolve into other genres? What other business opportunities like licensing, character development, commerce and other extensions could it generate over time?"

This means securing broader rights at earlier partnership stages. "Transmedia and derivative opportunities cannot be treated as afterthoughts," Yoon emphasized. "If you wait until a piece of content becomes a hit and successful, the timing is often too late. The trend shifts too quickly."

Kevin Mazur/Getty Images for iHeartRadio

Yoon agreed that Sony Pictures Animation’s _K-Pop Demon Hunters_ was an illustrative example of the timing challenge: the film became Netflix’s most-watched movie in history when it released in June 2025, but by the time its sequel arrives in 2029, the cultural moment that made the original resonate may have passed. CJ ENM’s new approach aims to lock in sequel, merchandising, and transmedia rights before a property proves itself, which is a risky move considering the earlier point about not being able to predict trends, but also allows for faster capitalization when hits do emerge.

The company is now "integrating transmedia planning and rights structuring from the earliest development phase so that expansion is embedded from the start, rather than thought of later."

Platform Growth and Consolidation
---------------------------------

The 2026 content budget — which Yoon confirmed would be "very similar" to the $818 million confirmed in 2025 to [Sara Merican for Deadline](https://deadline.com/2025/03/cj-enm-ceo-content-spend-severance-netflix-1236325191/) — continues the company’s strategy of allocating roughly 50% toward Korean drama production, with the remainder split among variety shows, music content, and film.

But Yoon made clear that growing digital platforms remains critical to gradually increasing future content investment. "Our strategy is to continue growing the subscriber base of our digital platforms, like TVING and Mnet Plus," he said. "By strengthening those platforms and expanding our recurring revenue, we aim to gradually increase our content investment over time."

TVING’s long-discussed merger with rival platform Wavve, which would create South Korea’s largest domestic streaming service, remains in progress with no clear timeline.

The platform did, however, make its first international moves in 2025 through branded partnerships. After [a deal](https://www.cjenm.com/en/news/warner-bros-discovery-and-cj-enm-ink-strategic-partnership/) with Warner Bros Discovery in October, TVING now appears as a content hub on HBO Max across 17 Asia-Pacific markets and on Disney+ in Japan. "Our immediate goal is to generate meaningful performance and more measurable and tangible success in those markets," Yoon said.

The same deal also created a “K-drama pipeline” for HBO Max with exclusive premieres on the platform. This was before Netflix announced its intention to [acquire Warner Bros Discovery](https://www.forbes.com/sites/siladityaray/2026/01/20/netflix-revises-warner-bros-deal-to-83-billion-all-cash-offer-to-fend-off-paramount/) in December 2025, a development that CJ ENM declined to comment on for this piece.

Global Expansion Beyond Content Sales
-------------------------------------

The company has already begun positioning for potential market access. In early February 2026, CJ ENM [announced ONECEAD](https://www.forbes.com/sites/laurasirikul/2026/02/05/cj-enm-jyp-china-and-tencent-music-entertainment-establish-onecead/), a joint venture with JYP CHINA and Tencent Music Entertainment focused on artist development and management in Greater China. The partnership builds on CJ ENM’s success with LAPONE Entertainment in Japan, which established artists like JO1 and INI. Despite ongoing restrictions, the Greater China market (including Hong Kong and Taiwan) represented K-pop's second-largest export market in 2023 at [$319.58 million](https://www.kocca.kr/kocca/bbs/view/B0158948/2009343.do?searchCnd=&searchWrd=&cateTp1=&cateTp2=&useYn=&menuNo=204156&categorys=0&subcate=0&cateCode=&type=&instNo=0&questionTp=&ufSetting=&recovery=&option1=&option2=&year=&morePage=&qtp=&domainId=&sortCode=&pageIndex=1).

The company also established CJ ENM Middle East LLC in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia in 2025, a market with no existing Korean diaspora infrastructure to build upon.

India, where I spoke to Yoon from, is "a market we continue to actively explore and engage with," according to the CEO, though he offered no specifics on potential partnerships or production plans.

The Lighthouse Fund and Asian Creator Development
-------------------------------------------------

In what may prove the most culturally significant initiative, CJ ENM Vice Chairwoman Miky Lee has established the First Light Storyhouse to support Asian creators globally. The fund aims to "develop projects together with these creators and help position Asian content, including K-content, as a major driver of global storytelling," Yoon explained.

When asked why Korean content specifically has achieved such global success, Yoon rejected the premise of a single explanation. "The reality is that there isn't a single explanation. There are many contributing factors," he said. "But one key element is the ability to discover compelling stories that can resonate globally while remaining authentic to their origins."

The Lighthouse Fund represents a bet that this model — culturally specific stories with universal resonance — can work for creators across Asia, not just Korea.

What Success Looks Like
-----------------------

When asked what his personal favorite K-drama was, Yoon laughed, looked around and said it was a sensitive subject. He relented after a couple of minutes though, naming _Our Unwritten Seoul_, a human growth drama that won recognition at the company’s internal Visionary Awards. "The choice reflects my individual taste, but I find stories about personal transformation and emotional development especially meaningful," he said.

It’s a preference that aligns with the company’s mid-budget strategy, which seems to involve elevated genre storytelling over spectacle, character development over visual effects budgets.

Can that thesis sustain an $818 million content budget in an increasingly crowded global market? That is yet to be seen. But with _Bugonia_ competing for Best Picture, _Bon Appétit, Your Majesty_ in Netflix's global top three, and platforms like TVING steadily gaining on Netflix in Korea, CJ ENM's bet on authentic storytelling over algorithmic formula is, at minimum, producing results that register far beyond Seoul.
